title: Can Agent Memory Systems Track Evolving State?
abstract: arXiv:2608.19652v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As LLM-based agents are deployed for longer and higher-stakes tasks, their memory systems continue to have crucial gaps. While existing memory benchmarks focus largely on recall-shaped tasks, we argue an effective memory system must track the evolving state of the world; as facts, constraints, and decisions are revised over a long interaction, answers must reflect the current state and not a superseded one. We define this capability as state tracking and instantiate it in StateMemBench, a benchmark of 234 multi-session scenarios spanning two conversation-length regimes. Its closed-pool grading scores whether an answer reflects the current state, the superseded state, or fails otherwise, separating state-tracking failures from other errors by construction. translated_title: 智能体记忆系统能否追踪不断变化的状态？
translated_abstract: 随着基于大语言模型的智能体被部署用于更长期、更高风险的任务，其记忆系统仍存在关键缺陷。虽然现有的记忆基准主要关注回忆型任务，但我们认为，一个有效的记忆系统必须追踪世界的动态变化；当事实、约束和决策在长时间交互中被修订时，答案必须反映当前状态，而非已被取代的状态。我们将这种能力定义为状态追踪，并在StateMemBench中实例化，这是一个包含234个多会话场景的基准，涵盖两种对话长度区间。其封闭池评分机制判断答案反映的是当前状态、被取代的状态还是其他失败，从而从构造上将状态追踪失败与其他错误区分开来。我们的分析表明，这一任务对现有记忆系统、检索增强基线和长上下文基线均具挑战性。随后，我们提出了StateMem，一种状态优先的记忆方法。
tldr: 本文提出状态追踪概念及StateMemBench基准，证明现有记忆系统难以追踪动态状态，并介绍StateMem方法以解决该问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces state tracking and the StateMemBench benchmark, demonstrating that existing memory systems struggle to track evolving states, and presents the StateMem method to address this challenge.
